findings.title: Bounded refuge against compelled inclination
findings.claim: The focus's threatened enclosure becomes a bounded refuge when it meets the next ayah's summons, heart-inclination, and ignorance: confinement can preserve agency against an inward movement the speaker fears.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries prison and protective holding, while 12:33 separately supplies the women's calling, inclination, and ignorance and places prison above that summons in Yusuf's comparison. Their contact reverses the threat's intended value without removing its ordinary punitive sense.
findings.reader_payoff: The prison word can be seen as a boundary that preserves the capacity not to be moved inwardly, as well as a loss of movement.
findings.containment: The reading keeps the threat, coercion, and abasement in view; it does not claim that prison is intrinsically safe or that every available branch of its roots is active.

epistemic.reason: A trusted channel nomination has exact focus and context contacts, but its source is evidence for local assessment rather than an adjudicated channel ledger.
